what_the_eye_sees: A plain, heavy gold band with a teardrop-shaped plaque standing up off one side. The plaque holds a round pierced medallion: about 16 petal-shaped (marquise) holes around a small round centre, so it looks like a daisy or sunflower. In the face view the band under the plaque looks like the bail ring on a pendant or a key fob. In the hero view the head sticks out from the band like a flag, not like part of the ring. The circular pierced wheel and the slightly pointed top of the plaque do suggest a round window, so a jeweller might guess 'rose window' on a second look. On first look, though, they would say 'flower medallion signet' or 'sunflower pendant ring'. Nothing says Gothic cathedral: there are no radial mullions, no pointed lancet heads, no cusps, no moulded frame and no arch. The rest of the band is blank metal.
changes: Wheel tracery (pierced medallion): replace the petal-shaped holes, which are pointed at both ends, with true wheel-window lights. Run 12 to 16 straight radial mullions, at least 0.9 mm wide, from a raised moulded hub (hub dia. about 3 mm, with a 0.3 mm roll) out to the rim. Give each light a pointed lancet head at the outer end and a trefoil cusp inside the head. Add a ring of small pierced roundels or quatrefoils (dia. about 1 mm) between the heads, just inside the rim. Acceptance: in face-300 the holes read as spokes and pointed arches, not petals.

Frame and silhouette of the plaque: wrap the wheel in a stepped outer moulding of 2 to 3 concentric orders (each about 0.5 to 0.6 mm wide, stepping down 0.3 mm). Redraw the plaque outline from a teardrop into a clear equilateral pointed-arch gable that rises at least 3 mm above the wheel, with a finial or crocket at the apex and straight sides down to the band. Acceptance: in face-300 the outline is a pointed arch framing a round window, not a teardrop.

Head integration and band: centre the window head on the crown so it sits square in the hero view instead of jutting off one side like a flag or bail. Sweep the shoulders up into the gable over at least 20° of theta each side. Carry the theme down the band with blind lancets or small pierced roundels on each shoulder (3 or more per side, graded) so the shank is not blank. Keep the wheel at 13 mm or more across. Acceptance: in hero-300 the head reads as part of the ring with Gothic ornament continuing down the shoulders, and the ring no longer reads as a pendant.
